# QS-CFW-2117-10 Quality specification - valve body CFW-2117-10 (F316)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-2117-10

Scope
This quality specification applies to valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10), forged from F316 grade material, manufactured at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forging, heat treat, and final machining handoff. Background and rationale are provided to ensure consistent evaluation and traceable records for customer quality and internal continuous improvement.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness | 39-44 HRC | Measured after final heat treat and stabilization |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.09 mm | Applies to final machined bore; measurement at part datum surfaces |
| Maximum forging weight | 14.5 kg | Weight measured after finishing flash removal, prior to machining |

Inspection method
General
- Inspectors shall verify each requirement listed in the Requirements table prior to release to machining or assembly. Rationale: early detection of deviations reduces scrap and rework and preserves heat treat control.

Hardness verification
- Method: Use a calibrated portable hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Measure on representative locations that are accessible without further machining and away from surface anomalies. Rationale: portable testers enable in-line verification while minimizing handling.
- Sampling and measurement protocol: For each part presented for hardness verification, take at least two readings on opposite faces or equivalent locations. If readings differ beyond allowed spread, perform a confirmatory test on a metallurgical coupon or a secondary location on the same part. Rationale: multi-point verification reduces false failures due to localized work hardening or surface condition.
- Acceptance: Part is acceptable only if readings fall within 39-44 HRC across verified locations. Record all readings in the inspection record.

Bore diameter verification
- Method: Use calibrated bore gauge equipment or coordinate measuring equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measure at a nominally mid-depth location along the bore and at defined datum references. Rationale: bore tolerance is critical for fit and sealing; measurement must reference the same datums used by machining.
- Acceptance: The measured bore diameter must be within ±0.09 mm of nominal drawing size. If the bore is out of tolerance, part shall be segregated and processed as nonconforming.
- Example: If a gauge indicates deviation beyond ±0.09 mm at any evaluated plane, record measurement and follow nonconformance handling.

Forging weight verification
- Method: Weigh each forging after flash removal and trimming using calibrated scales. Record weight on the material traveler and inspection form.
- Acceptance: Weight must not exceed 14.5 kg. Parts under the maximum are acceptable provided all other requirements are met. Rationale: maximum forging weight controls cycle loads and material use and confirms correct batch processing.

Surface condition and visual
- Method: Visual inspection for defects that could affect function or machinability. Remove loose scale prior to inspection. Rationale: superficial defects may mask subsurface issues; visual checks help prevent tooling damage.
- Acceptance: Defects that compromise intended use or prevent attainment of dimensional features shall be documented and treated as nonconformance.

Records to keep
- For each inspected part, retain the following records in the document control system and on the material traveler:
  - Hardness readings with tester identification and calibration status.
  - Bore diameter measurements with instrument identification and calibration status.
  - Weighing result and scale identification.
  - Visual inspection notes and photographic evidence where anomalies exist.
  - Inspector name or badge identifier and timestamp of inspection.
- Rationale: complete records ensure traceability for customer inquiries, warranty claims, and process improvement.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part failing to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be immediately tagged and segregated from conforming material. Rationale: prevents inadvertent use and facilitates root cause analysis.

Disposition options
- Rework: If a nonconformance is deemed recoverable by authorized engineering, a rework instruction shall be issued and the part shall be re-inspected following the rework. Re-inspection must include all applicable checks from this specification.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be restored to meet requirements or that exceed safe material limits shall be scrapped in accordance with Plant P2 scrap procedures.
- Return to process owner: For issues originating in forging or heat treat, parts may be returned to the originating operation for containment and corrective action.

Reporting and corrective action
- All nonconformances shall be recorded in the nonconformance report system with supporting data from Records to keep. Rationale: structured reporting enables trending and process improvement.
- Engineering review is required for repeated failures against any single requirement to determine root cause and necessary process controls or design reviews.

Examples
- Example nonconformance scenario: A forging measures 41 HRC at one location and 45 HRC at another location. Action: segregate part, perform confirmatory hardness testing, initiate nonconformance report, and quarantine similar parts from the same heat for inspection.
- Example disposition: A bore found beyond ±0.09 mm may be evaluated for undersize salvage via insert or sleeve only after engineering approval. If no restorative path is approved, designate part as scrap.

Roles and responsibilities
- Quality inspectors: execute inspections and maintain records.
- Process owners: implement containment for detected deviations and coordinate corrective actions.
- Engineering: review nonconformance trends and approve dispositions that alter part geometry or material condition.

This specification is mandatory for all valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) production at Plant P2. Compliance ensures fit, function, and service life consistent with customer expectations.
